title: The architect-facing results slice (the presentation contract's step 3): the Results tool shows the property's identity, the three answers in the order label, value, exception, details, one option comparison, and every data state, on the shared tokens, at desktop and phone widths
objective: Rebuild the Results tool to the owner's presentation contract for the benchmark lot and every data state: identity first; one context strip of at most three items; the three answers together, each as label, value or unavailable state, one exception, details; 'Building option: site fit not verified' with the scheduled area; one option comparison with the same rows, order and units, a not-worked building as 'Not known' never 0; shared conditions once; at most three notices; two columns at desktop and one at 320 to 700 px; focus and keyboard behaviour; no developer words.
business_reason: The owner's brief: the first screen must make the useful answer, its basis and its material limitation understandable at once; the full evidence stays available. The walkthrough notes N1 to N3 (DB-214) and the screen wordings (DB-215 b) are closed here.
inputs: the adapters and tokens of M5-T148
D-090 source-080 (the owner's review: rows R894, R895)
outputs: the rebuilt Results tool and its tests
a browser layout test at six widths

acceptance_scenarios.input: the benchmark lot at 1440 x 900, the Results tool open
acceptance_scenarios.expected: two columns: the answers at 40 to 48 percent of the window's width and at least 320 px, the details on the right; the lot, the program and the floor height are visible without scrolling (UX-01).

acceptance_scenarios.input: 320, 390, 768, 1024, 1440 and 1920 px; 200 percent zoom and the text-spacing check at 1280 px
acceptance_scenarios.expected: no sideways page scroll; no clipped text outside labelled scroll regions; 16 px padding at 700 px and below (UX-07, UX-08).
the strip shows the document's status_strip items, at most three; shared conditions are stated once; at most three notices show at once, the rest behind a count (UX-04).

acceptance_scenarios.input: every result on the benchmark lot
acceptance_scenarios.expected: label, then the value or 'Not known'/'Not available', then at most one exception, then Details; Details moves focus into its region; Escape returns focus to the opener (UX-09).

acceptance_scenarios.case: Legal limit apart from the estimate (DB-214 N2)
acceptance_scenarios.input: the benchmark lot with the special-density statement made
acceptance_scenarios.expected: '29 units' appears only with the floor-area allowance, marked Conditional; '17.27 to 21.59' appears only with the building option, tagged as an estimate (UX-02, UX-14).

acceptance_scenarios.case: Building option first, scheduled not achieved
acceptance_scenarios.input: the benchmark lot at 10 ft; at 16 ft
acceptance_scenarios.expected: at 10 ft: 'Building option: site fit not verified' with 'Scheduled area: 20,150 sq ft' and the document's not_checked items; the word 'achieved' appears nowhere (row R895). At 16 ft: no scheduled area; each building's reason from the document.

acceptance_scenarios.input: the benchmark lot; the synthetic two-building test document
acceptance_scenarios.expected: buildings side by side with the same rows, order and units; a not-worked building reads 'Not known' with its reason, never 0; one wording per situation (row R894); at 700 px and below, stacked summaries with the table in a labelled scroll region (UX-06, UX-14).
the normal state shows three headline values with units; the partial state shows the withheld results as 'Not known' with the kind of gap and no number (UX-02, UX-03).
a notice that names what is missing, no number, no 'safe to retry' (UX-03, UX-13).

acceptance_scenarios.case: Failed fetch, stale answer, another lot
acceptance_scenarios.input: a network error; a slow first answer overtaken by a second; a changed input; a document for another lot
acceptance_scenarios.expected: a notice with retry; only the newest answer shows; a stale answer is marked stale; another lot's document is not shown (UX-05).

acceptance_scenarios.input: the loading, empty, partial, error and normal states
acceptance_scenarios.expected: a text check finds no field name, code, route, contract version, task id or raw state word; the measurement-basis words of the estimate are tied to the contract's text by a test (DB-215 b) (UX-13).

risks: Part A moves the building-option styles (three-answers.css lines 373 to 547) to Part B's new building-options.css: both parts must agree the move, and the CSS import moves with FirstBuildingOptions.tsx.
The comparison depends on the owner's open question A2; it is built under its meanwhile rule (every building, none preferred).
path_notes:
PARTS: A (the answers, the strip, the scope summary, the details and shared conditions; three-answers.css), B (the building options, the comparison, building-options.css, the view model's building part, the synthetic two-building test document) and C (the Results window and form, the wide-window list in DashboardEntry, the window CSS, the browser tests) share no file and run side by side after M5-T148 is integrated. FirstBuildingOptions keeps its props, so Part A's journey test only checks that Part B's section is present.

THE ORCHESTRATOR'S RULINGS FOR WAVE 20 (they govern; later over earlier). V1: three tasks on ONE branch, reviewed at ONE head, merged as ONE pull request: M5-T148 (shared presentation), M5-T149 (the website slice, after M5-T148) and M5-T150 (the parcel's own outline; server only, beside M5-T148). Order: M5-T148 parts A and B and M5-T150 side by side (three builders, disjoint files); integrate; then M5-T149 parts A, B and C side by side (three builders); then the orchestrator builds the website, runs the browser tests (stopping the owner's preview for the run and restarting it), takes the pictures and starts the reviews. V2: the website types no number, label, condition or reason; the presentation adapters only format numbers and group what the document says; they decide no law and recalculate nothing (D-090 R855). V3: the screen's statuses stay as the owner decided (row R641: 'Preliminary zoning results'; settled, conditional, not known); the owner's question C2 (the PDF's six labels on the screen) is open; 'Verified' is never shown. V4: the font token equals the application's existing font stack (`apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx`); no font changes in this wave. V5: a floor schedule whose placement and site fit are not established is never called 'achieved' (row R895): it is the 'scheduled area', with 'site fit not verified' beside it, before any caveat; the option comparison uses ONE wording per situation (row R894). V6: builders never start Next, Playwright or any server, and never touch ports 3000, 3001 or 8000 (the owner's preview); the orchestrator runs the browser tests. V7: a builder who finds that a file outside its part must change STOPS and reports. V8: nothing is called feasible, compliant, verified, optimal or preferred; a withheld value shows no number anywhere. V9: the estimate on the benchmark lot is 17.27 to 21.59 apartments (from the document); the planning draft's '22.20' was wrong.
documented_test_commands: cd apps/web && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npx vitest run src/components/architect src/lib
the browser tests and the layout test are run by the orchestrator (ruling V6)
